buildingFundamentals.title: Frame and load path
buildingFundamentals.principle: The frame carries every impact from wheels, tools, cargo, and terrain. Reinforce where force enters the creation instead of covering the whole build in heavy material.
checklist: Keep the center of mass low and between the main contact points.
Reinforce bearing mounts, suspension towers, tool heads, and tow points.
Leave engines, controllers, fuel, and critical connections reachable.

buildingFundamentals.title: Motion and power
buildingFundamentals.principle: A moving creation needs an input, a power or timing part, and a mechanical output. Build that chain in the open before bodywork hides it.
checklist: Seat or switch → engine or controller → bearing, piston, or thruster.
Start with low power and verify rotation or extension direction.
Include a stopped state that remains safe when the player exits.

buildingFundamentals.title: Steering and stability
buildingFundamentals.principle: Wheelbase, track width, mass, steering angle, suspension, and engine power work as one system. Tune them with the normal cargo already loaded.
checklist: Test full steering lock without wheels touching the chassis.
Reduce speed before adding weight to solve flipping.
Check braking and reverse control on a slope, not only on flat ground.

buildingFundamentals.title: Signals and automation
buildingFundamentals.principle: A reliable machine has readable inputs, logic, outputs, and reset behavior. Complex timing should be added only after every physical movement works manually.
checklist: Test Buttons, Switches, Seats, and Sensors one at a time.
Use the Connect Tool to follow the complete signal chain.
Mark manual override, stop, and reset controls with consistent colors.

buildingFundamentals.title: Recovery and service
buildingFundamentals.principle: A build is not finished until it can be stopped, lifted, unloaded, and repaired after a failure away from the base.
checklist: Keep at least one useful Lift point clear.
Separate valuable cargo from impact and moving tools.
Carry a small repair reserve without loading the entire workshop.

buildFailureChecks.inspect: Center of mass, track width, speed, suspension travel
buildFailureChecks.firstChange: Lower heavy parts or reduce power before adding armor

buildFailureChecks.inspect: Bearing direction, wheel contact, steering angle, frame flex
buildFailureChecks.firstChange: Raise the build and test each steering joint slowly

buildFailureChecks.inspect: Contact angle, chassis mass, joint stiffness, driver visibility
buildFailureChecks.firstChange: Control tool pressure instead of ramming the target

buildFailureChecks.inspect: Input state, connection path, collision, controller sequence
buildFailureChecks.firstChange: Return to manual movement and test one output at a time

buildFailureChecks.inspect: Cargo position, suspension load, engine power, braking distance
buildFailureChecks.firstChange: Tune with normal cargo placed low inside the wheelbase
